title: fix-network verification
description: How the tool is checked. Every command, lookup and connection goes through the Sys trait, so the tests drive the whole tool (gathering, diagnosis, each repair step, both commands) against a scripted Mac, and the real implementation against localhost. Results and coverage figures are readings and are not kept here.

entities.title: Both commands against a scripted Mac
entities.summary: diagnose and fix run end to end through main.rs's run on sys::fake::Fake, a Mac whose command answers, names, open ports, clock and SSH flag are scripted.
criteria: Repeated --internal-host and the fix flags parse; a bad port is refused
Anything but macOS is refused with status 2 before any command runs
A healthy diagnosis exits 0, runs no sudo and no Wi-Fi change, and saves original.json
A broken VPN service exits 1 and names fix --vpn
A state directory that cannot be created exits 1
fix on a healthy Mac runs nothing and exits 0
fix --vpn reconnects the VPN, verifies the intranet again and exits 0 without cycling Wi-Fi
A failed reconnect exits 1, is logged FAILED and ends in manual advice
Dry runs change nothing and list blocked steps; the --force ladder comes first without repeats
A Mac with no network service still produces a diagnosis

entities.title: Diagnosis scenarios
entities.summary: assess.rs and corp.rs judge hand-built snapshots of healthy and broken Macs, and facts.rs gathers snapshots from the scripted Mac.
criteria: A healthy network has no findings and leaves corporate checks NOT TESTED
Healthy public internet does not hide a broken VPN service
A corporate DNS failure with a dead VPN DNS server suggests a VPN reconnect, not Wi-Fi
A resolver fault answered directly by the server escalates from a flush to a reboot
An internal host routed outside the tunnel is a routing failure
A dead full tunnel is blamed instead of the Wi-Fi; two tunnels claiming the default route are a conflict
A third-party tunnel is UNSUPPORTED, never HEALTHY
Stale VPN state after sleep is tagged with the wake time
Unreachable proxies are fixable; a dead PAC file is manual
A name resolving to a sinkhole address is flagged
Gathering reads hung configd, missing dig, IPv6-only and wired Macs correctly

checks.description: The scenario tests in module tests, for example test_assess_public_ok_vpn_broken, test_assess_full_tunnel_dead, test_assess_third_party_tunnel and test_assess_stale_after_wake.
The corporate DNS, corporate service and proxy scenarios in module tests.
Gathering against the scripted Mac and the snapshot helpers, in module tests.

entities.title: Gates, plan, fix loop and every repair step
entities.summary: repair.rs's tests check the gates, the plan's order, the fix loop and each step's commands and failures against the scripted Mac.
criteria: Gated steps need their flag; over SSH, disruptive steps need --allow-remote
Plans are deduplicated, sorted least disruptive first and skip manual remedies
A healthy network runs no step without --force; --force runs the ladder and skips what SSH blocks
A VPN-only fault reconnects the VPN and never cycles Wi-Fi; without --vpn it runs nothing and names the flag
A failed step is logged FAILED and the loop moves on
Each step reports success, and failure with the command, including Wi-Fi that stays off and a watchdog that cannot start
VPN reconnects succeed through stop and start, and fail when the VPN never disconnects or never connects

entities.title: Parsers against documented output formats
entities.summary: parse.rs's tests parse fixtures written to follow documented macOS output formats for netstat, scutil, networksetup, ifconfig, sysctl and dig, and the --internal-host forms.
criteria: Routes parse in both families, with and without the older Refs and Use columns
Split-DNS and scoped resolvers, IPv6 nameservers, proxies, VPN lists and states, services and interfaces parse
Targets parse as HOST, HOST:PORT, [V6]:PORT and bare IPv6; junk is refused

checks.description: The fixture tests in module tests.

entities.details: The fixtures were not captured from a real Mac: see limitations.json, scripted-not-real.

entities.title: The real Sys implementation against localhost
entities.summary: sys.rs's tests run Real against this machine without touching its network settings: sudo prefixing, bounded commands, name lookups, TCP to a local listener, the clock and the watchdog script.
criteria: sudo is added only when not root, with -n when there is no terminal
Commands return their exit code and combined output, time out with 124 and report a missing binary as 127
Lookups handle literals, localhost, empty answers, errors and timeouts
TCP succeeds against a local listener and fails against port 1, where nothing listens (a freed ephemeral port could be reused as the client's own source port)
The watchdog script runs, logs, and quotes the device name

entities.title: Session, log and redaction
entities.summary: run.rs's tests check the state root, the private state directory, the log, redaction of secret-looking lines and original.json.
criteria: FIXNET_STATE overrides the state root; otherwise it is under HOME
Lines assigning a password, PSK or token are dropped; ordinary lines mentioning a password are kept
The state directory is mode 0700 and original.json is written
Colour only on a terminal without NO_COLOR

entities.title: Branch and line coverage gate
entities.summary: CI fails when fix-network's non-test line or branch coverage drops below 95%; test modules are kept out of the figures.
criteria: At least 95% of lines and of branches are covered, test code excluded

checks.symbol: fix-network needs 95% line and branch coverage

entities.details: Each test module carries `#[cfg_attr(coverage_nightly, coverage(off))]`, and `Cargo.toml` declares the `coverage_nightly` cfg that cargo llvm-cov sets.
